title: The mean of eight
starter:
%x  = buffer 8 dtype=f32 slot=0
%m  = buffer 1 dtype=f32 slot=1
# m[0] = (x[0] + ... + x[7]) * 0.125
%v  = load %x
%s  = reduce %v op=add
%mv = shrink %m 0 shape=[]
%st = store %mv %s
%m1 = after %m %st
hints: The starter stores the sum. The mean is the sum times one eighth.
Multiply the reduced scalar by `0.125` (exact in f32) before storing it.
Don't reorder the sum: `reduce` folds left to right from `x[0]`, and the tests with `1e8` check that order bit for bit.
explain: The sum folds left to right from the first element, so `1e8 + 1 + ... + 1 - 1e8` loses every 1 (each `1e8 + 1` rounds back to `1e8`) and the mean is 0, while putting `-1e8` second keeps all six ones. Overflow is real too: `3e38 + 3e38` is `inf` in f32, so the mean is `inf`. Eight `-0.0`s sum to `-0.0`, because the fold starts from `x[0]`, not from `+0.0`.
